items.title: Baer's criterion produces functorial injective embeddings for modules
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file injectives.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The theorem states that for a cardinal larger than the number of ideals and an ordinal of larger cofinality, the module constructed by the transfinite process is injective and receives a functorial injective embedding from any module (statement lines 566-572). The proof is a complete argument: Baer's criterion reduces the claim to extending maps from ideals (proof lines 574-577); the extension is produced by pushing the given map one step further in the construction and using the defining property of the functor M (proof lines 577-602); and the cofinality hypothesis keeps the extension inside the stage considered, which gives injectivity and, with functoriality of the construction, the functorial embedding (proof lines 602-608). The non-formal content is the one-step extension argument. The claim is H2.
